discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Shaun Cole
nominees.affiliation: Durham University, Institute for Computational Cosmology, UK

nominees.name: John A. Peacock
nominees.affiliation: University of Edinburgh, Institute for Astronomy, UK

motivation: In 2005 two independent galaxy surveys, SDSS (led in this analysis by Eisenstein) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Peacock and collaborators), detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies. This feature is the same acoustic physics seen in the cosmic microwave background, frozen into matter at recombination. The detection confirmed that cosmic structure grew gravitationally from small adiabatic fluctuations in a universe dominated by cold dark matter, joining the early and late universe in one quantitative framework. Eisenstein's theoretical work made the acoustic scale a precise standard ruler. Baryon acoustic oscillations have since become one of the most robust probes of cosmic geometry and dark energy, culminating in BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, whose recent results hint at evolving dark energy. This discovery changed how physicists measure the contents and expansion history of the universe.
